name: Demetrius and the silversmiths of Ephesus
charge: Raising an uproar over lost trade under the colour of zeal for Diana
summary: Demetrius called the craftsmen together and told them plainly what was at stake — Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth — then dressed the grievance up as danger to the temple of the great goddess. The city filled with confusion for two hours, and the townclerk sent them home.
offense: A certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen. He called them together and said that Paul had persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands: so that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought, but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised. They were full of wrath, and the whole city was filled with confusion, and they caught Gaius and Aristarchus and rushed into the theatre.
judgment: No sentence is recorded upon Demetrius. The townclerk appeased the people and gave the verdict the law would have given: ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly; for ye have brought hither these men, which are neither robbers of churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddess. If Demetrius, and the craftsmen which are with him, have a matter against any man, the law is open, and there are deputies: let them implead one another. And he warned them they were in danger to be called in question for this day's uproar, there being no cause — then dismissed the assembly.

entries.commentary: An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. The priests were given linen breeches to cover their nakedness from the loins even unto the thighs when they came near the altar, and Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests, so do not be simple and say that law was only for Aaron and his sons. Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows.

Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant, and Israel whom I have chosen; thus saith the Lord that made thee and formed thee from the womb and will help thee. Fear not, for I will pour water upon him that is thirsty and floods upon the dry ground, and pour my spirit upon thy seed and my blessing upon thine offspring. They shall spring up as among the grass, as willows by the watercourses. One shall say I am the Lord's, another shall call himself by the name of Jacob, and another shall subscribe with his hand unto the Lord and surname himself by the name of Israel. This is prophecy of our name being changed back: on the sabbath classes a member is announced no longer a Corinthian or an Ephesian, because they take a pen and legalize their name change, subscribing with the hand as the scripture said. -

Thus saith the Lord the King of Israel and his redeemer the Lord of hosts: I am the first and I am the last, and beside me there is no God. Who as I shall call and declare it and set it in order, since I appointed the ancient people? Fear ye not, neither be afraid; have not I told thee from that time and declared it? Ye are even my witnesses. Is there a God beside me? Yea, there is no God, I know not any. Our God stays bragging through the bible that he knows no other God. -

They that make a graven image are all of them vanity, their delectable things shall not profit, and they are their own witnesses; they see not nor know, that they may be ashamed. Who has formed a god or molten a graven image profitable for nothing? The smith works it in the coals and fashions it with hammers, working with the strength of his arms until he is hungry and his strength fails; the carpenter stretches out his rule, marks it with a compass, and makes it after the figure of a man. Same as Jeremiah said, they fasten idols with nails so they move not and must be carried, so how can it have power? He heweth down cedars, cypress, and oak, which grow among the trees of the forest; part of the same tree he burns to warm himself and bake bread, and the residue he maketh a god and worshippeth it, falling down and praying deliver me, for thou art my god. He uses the same wood to warm himself yet thinks the rest is a god.

They have not known nor understood, for he hath shut their eyes that they cannot see and their hearts that they cannot understand. None considereth in his heart to say I have burned part in the fire and roasted flesh, so shall I make the residue an abomination and fall down to the stock of a tree? This is the strong delusion: our people are convinced color does not matter, so it is easy for a white jesus to sit in the temple and show himself to be god, when Christ is shown black from the scripture. He feedeth on ashes, a deceived heart hath turned him aside, and he cannot deliver his soul nor say, is there not a lie in my right hand? -

Remember these, O Jacob and Israel, for thou art my servant; I have formed thee, thou shalt not be forgotten of me. I have blotted out as a thick cloud thy transgressions and as a cloud thy sins; return unto me, for I have redeemed thee. Repentance is for Israel; when he blots out the sins he is speaking of Jacob, the servants that sinned whom God is calling back. Sing O ye heavens, shout ye lower parts of the earth, break forth into singing, for the Lord hath redeemed Jacob and glorified himself in Israel. -

Thus saith the Lord thy redeemer that formed thee from the womb: I am the Lord that maketh all things, that stretcheth forth the heavens alone and spreadeth abroad the earth by myself. There is no God beside our God. He frustrateth the tokens of the liars and maketh diviners mad, turning wise men backward and making their knowledge foolish, for the wisdom of the world is foolishness to God. He confirmeth the word of his servant and performeth the counsel of his messengers. That saith to Jerusalem, thou shalt be inhabited, and to the cities of Judah, ye shall be built, raising up the decayed places. That saith of Cyrus, he is my shepherd and shall perform all my pleasure, saying to Jerusalem thou shalt be built and to the temple thy foundation shall be laid. Jerusalem will be the place where Christ's feet touch down and Israel rules the world, not the gentiles trodding it down now.

verses.text: And the same time there arose no small stir about that way.
For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen;
Whom he called together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth.
Moreover ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands:

So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth.
And when they heard these sayings, they were full of wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
And the whole city was filled with confusion: and having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel, they rushed with one accord into the theatre.

And when the townclerk had appeased the people, he said, Ye men of Ephesus, what man is there that knoweth not how that the city of the Ephesians is a worshipper of the great goddess Diana, and of the image which fell down from Jupiter?
Seeing then that these things cannot be spoken against, ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.
For ye have brought hither these men, which are neither robbers of churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddess.
Wherefore if Demetrius, and the craftsmen which are with him, have a matter against any man, the law is open, and there are deputies: let them implead one another.
But if ye enquire any thing concerning other matters, it shall be determined in a lawful assembly.
For we are in danger to be called in question for this day’s uproar, there being no cause whereby we may give an account of this concourse.
And when he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.
Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:
They that make a graven image are all of them vanity; and their delectable things shall not profit; and they are their own witnesses; they see not, nor know; that they may be ashamed.
Who hath formed a god, or molten a graven image that is profitable for nothing?
Behold, all his fellows shall be ashamed: and the workmen, they are of men: let them all be gathered together, let them stand up; yet they shall fear, and they shall be ashamed together.
